claudeConfig.disableArtifactHelp: Leaves the Artifact tool out of requests. Some third-party gateways reject its schema and return 400 on every request. Switches with the provider.
claudeConfig.disableAutoModeServerHelp: Gateways can't run the server-side check, so auto mode pauses once per session with a "not eligible" notice, then falls back to the local check after you press Enter. Checked, it uses the local check right away with no notice. Leave it unchecked on official endpoints.
claudeConfig.disableAutoUpgradeHelp: Keeps Claude Code on its current version instead of updating automatically; run claude update yourself when needed. Global.
claudeConfig.enableToolSearchHelp: Loads MCP tool definitions on demand to save context. Off by default on third-party endpoints; enable it only if the upstream supports tool_reference. Switches with the provider.
claudeConfig.hideAttributionHelp: Commits and PRs created by Claude Code no longer carry the Co-Authored-By trailer or the session link. Global: applies to every provider.

codexConfig.advancedSectionHint: Includes upstream format, model mapping, reasoning overrides and custom User-Agent. Providers using the Chat Completions protocol require routing takeover to be enabled.
codexConfig.anthropicAuthFieldHint: Choose which header carries the API key to the gateway: ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN sends Authorization: Bearer; ANTHROPIC_API_KEY sends x-api-key. Only one is sent.
codexConfig.authJsonStorageHint: In Routing mode this shows the stored auth, not the live auth.json.
codexConfig.autoCompactLimitHint: Auto-compacts history when context reaches this token limit
codexConfig.configTomlStorageHint: In Routing mode this shows the stored config, not the live config.toml.
codexConfig.defaultModelHint: The model Codex requests by default; change it anytime without waiting for a preset update. If left empty while model mapping is configured, the first mapping row is used.
codexConfig.defaultModelNotInCatalog: This model is not in the model mapping, so the Codex /model menu won't list it (direct requests still work).
codexConfig.impersonateClaudeCodeHint: Enable when the gateway (or its upstream) restricts usage to Claude Code: spoofs the User-Agent, anthropic-beta and x-app headers, and injects the Claude Code identity as the first system prompt line.
codexConfig.inactiveFieldsHint: This provider still stores {{count}} settings that are not applied when switching. Click one to copy its TOML and paste it above if you need it; the stored values are kept.
codexConfig.keyFieldsHint: The endpoint, key, model, reasoning effort, context window and compatibility switches follow the provider; everything else is a global Codex setting that applies to every provider once saved.
codexConfig.maxOutputTokensHint: Codex does not forward model_max_output_tokens in the request body, so the default 8192 ceiling can truncate long or thinking-heavy responses (stop_reason=max_tokens). This value overrides the request's max_tokens on the Anthropic path. Do not exceed the real output ceiling of the model/gateway or it may 400. Leave empty to use the default 8192.
codexConfig.maxOutputTokensPlaceholder: Leave empty to use the default 8192
codexConfig.modelListEmpty: No models configured: in Aggregation mode only this provider's default model (the model in config.toml) is published.
codexConfig.modelMappingHint: Generates Codex model_catalog_json so /model can show these third-party model names; entries are saved exactly as listed. Codex must be restarted to refresh the model list after changes.
codexConfig.modelMetadataAdvancedHint: Overrides Codex metadata for unknown models; clearing a field removes the matching config.toml entry.
codexConfig.modelNameHint: Specify the model to use, will be auto-updated in config.toml
codexConfig.promptCacheRoutingHint: Auto sends prompt_cache_key only to known-compatible upstreams. Enable it for other compatible gateways, or disable it if a strict gateway rejects unknown fields with HTTP 400. Only a stable client-provided session ID is used.
codexConfig.proxyTakeoverStorageNotice: 💡 This app is in Routing mode. You are editing the stored provider config; the live config is temporarily managed by the routing service.
codexConfig.reasoningEffortHint: Enable when the upstream supports thinking-depth control such as low/high/max. Enabling this also turns on thinking mode and converts Codex's reasoning.effort into the upstream Chat parameter.
codexConfig.reasoningModeHint: Enable when the upstream Chat Completions API supports toggling thinking on/off. Providers like Kimi, GLM and Qwen usually fall into this category.
codexConfig.reasoningSectionHint: Preset providers are configured automatically; custom providers are inferred from name/URL. Override manually only when auto-detection is wrong.
codexConfig.remoteCompactionHint: When enabled, the active model_providers entry name is written as OpenAI so Codex can try remote compaction.
codexConfig.stackAdvancedHint: Reasoning, Anthropic-specific options, custom User-Agent and request overrides; usually no need to change.
codexConfig.stackDefaultNotInList: The default model {{model}} is not in the list: Codex still requests it by default, but /model won't show it.
codexConfig.stackModelListHint: These models appear in Codex's /model menu; picking one sends requests straight to this provider. The one marked ★ is this provider's default model: while this provider is the default, Codex uses it by default. Restart Codex after changes.
codexConfig.upstreamFormatCopilotHint: Automatic mode prefers Responses when supported by the model, otherwise Chat Completions. You can also select a protocol explicitly; models that do not support it will return an error. All modes require Codex routing takeover to inject Copilot account credentials.
codexConfig.upstreamFormatHint: Pick Responses when your provider is natively a Responses API (direct, no format conversion); pick Chat when it uses the Chat Completions protocol; pick Anthropic Messages when it only offers the native Anthropic Messages protocol. Chat and Anthropic Messages both require routing takeover to convert to Responses.
codexConfig.upstreamModelNameHint: For Chat format, enter the real upstream model here; routing converts Codex Responses requests to Chat Completions while keeping this model.

agentTooltip.atlas: Main orchestrator (holds TODO list) responsible for task distribution and coordination during execution phase. Delegates to specialized agents rather than completing all work directly.
agentTooltip.explore: Fast codebase exploration and context grep expert. Uses lightweight models for high-speed search. The scout for understanding code structure.
agentTooltip.hephaestus: Autonomous deep worker ("legitimate craftsman") inspired by AmpCode deep mode. Goal-oriented execution that launches 2-5 explore/librarian agents in parallel for research before taking action.
agentTooltip.librarian: Multi-repository analysis and documentation retrieval expert. Deeply understands codebases and provides evidence-based answers. Excels at finding official documentation and open-source implementation examples.
agentTooltip.metis: Plan consultant that performs pre-analysis before planning. Identifies hidden intents, ambiguities and AI failure points to prevent over-engineering.
agentTooltip.momus: Plan reviewer that validates plan clarity, verifiability and completeness with high precision. Rejects and requests revisions until plans are perfect.
agentTooltip.multimodalLooker: Visual content expert that analyzes PDFs, images, charts and other non-text media, extracting information and insights from them.
agentTooltip.oracle: Architecture decision and debugging advisor. Read-only consulting agent providing excellent logical reasoning and deep analysis. Cannot write files or delegate tasks.
agentTooltip.prometheus: Strategic planner that collects requirements through interview mode and creates detailed work plans. Can only read/write Markdown files in .sisyphus/ directory, never writes code directly.
agentTooltip.sisyphus: Main orchestrator responsible for task planning, delegation and parallel execution. Uses extended thinking (32k budget) and drives workflows through TODO lists to ensure task completion.
agentTooltip.sisyphusJunior: Category-generated executor, automatically created via category parameters. Focuses on executing assigned tasks and cannot re-delegate, preventing infinite delegation loops.

categoryTooltip.artistry: Highly creative and artistic task category that inspires novel ideas and creative solutions. Defaults to Gemini 3.6 Flash high variant.
categoryTooltip.deep: Deep autonomous problem-solving category with goal-oriented execution. Conducts thorough research before action, suitable for difficult problems requiring deep understanding.
categoryTooltip.quick: Lightweight task category for single-file modifications, typo fixes, and simple adjustments. Defaults to Claude Haiku 4.5 fast model.
categoryTooltip.ultrabrain: Deep logical reasoning category for complex architectural decisions requiring extensive analysis. Defaults to GPT-5.3 Codex ultra-high reasoning variant.
categoryTooltip.unspecifiedHigh: Uncategorized high-effort task category for tasks that don't fit other categories with large workload. Defaults to Claude Opus 5 max variant.
categoryTooltip.unspecifiedLow: Uncategorized low-effort task category for tasks that don't fit other categories with small workload. Defaults to Claude Sonnet 4.5.
categoryTooltip.visualEngineering: Frontend and visual engineering category for UI/UX design, styling, animation and interface implementation. Defaults to Gemini 3.6 Flash model.
categoryTooltip.writing: Writing category for documentation, prose and technical writing. Defaults to Kimi K2.5 model.

Only requests through the routing service with at least 100 output tokens count; for models that hide their reasoning it's an approximation. A value with ≈ is estimated from session-log timestamps when routing is off: there is no first-token timing, so the wait for the first token is included and the number reads low. Only requests with at least 200 output tokens are estimated.
usage.speedSumHelp: Total output tokens divided by total generation time, not an average of per-request speeds, so short requests don't skew it. Only requests through the routing service with at least 100 output tokens count. A value with ≈ is estimated from session logs (it includes the wait for the first token, and only requests with at least 200 output tokens count) and is shown only when the row has no routed data.
